source_identity: CFA UK Certificate in Climate and Investing curriculum supplied by the user
publication_edition: Not independently established. Core reviewed passages refer to 2021 materials.
page_convention: One-indexed PDF pages. Printed page numbers restart by chapter; never substitute printed labels for PDF offsets.
review_scope: Targeted operational conversion, not an exhaustive review of all 897 pages. Chapter introductions/contents mapped; selected investment, data, scenario, stewardship and client sections reviewed. No source text or page images redistributed.

chapters.title: Introduction to Climate and Investing
chapters.workflow_use: Mandate framing, mitigation/adaptation/resilience and instrument differences.

chapters.title: Climate science and climate risks and considerations
chapters.workflow_use: Physical and transition risk; hazard, exposure, vulnerability; uncertainty and natural capital.

chapters.title: Regulation, policy response and the corporate reporting landscape
chapters.workflow_use: Historical policy/disclosure framework; date-specific verification is required for use today.

chapters.title: Climate change impacts and opportunities
chapters.workflow_use: Financial transmission, sector opportunities, mitigation, adaptation and resilience.

chapters.title: Climate risk measurement: data, metrics, targets and scenario analysis
chapters.workflow_use: Evidence quality, emissions, targets, model selection, scenario analysis and its limits.

chapters.title: Stewardship and engagement on climate
chapters.workflow_use: Investor engagement, milestones and monitoring; external actions need separate approval.

chapters.title: Listed investment instruments
chapters.workflow_use: Primary equity, bond, labelled debt and listed real-asset integration.

chapters.title: Climate change and private markets
chapters.workflow_use: Context only: private-market and underlying real-asset differences; not a private-market execution module.

chapters.title: Portfolio management
chapters.workflow_use: Mandate-aware construction, climate metrics, benchmarks and attribution.

chapters.title: Serving client needs
chapters.workflow_use: Client mandate, accountability, investor disclosure and review.

anchors.method: Physical/transition risks, mitigation/adaptation, instrument structure and climate versus ESG.
Hazard is not loss: exposure, vulnerability, supply chains and stranded assets/liabilities.
Policy/reporting context and explicit warning that regulatory material is time-sensitive.
Revenues, expenditure, assets/liabilities, capital/financing and free cash flows.
Resource efficiency, energy source, products/services, markets and resilience.
Data gaps, comparability, reporting boundaries, granular locations and transparent methods.
Scope aggregation, activity/revenue intensity, WACI and limitations.
Climate models, IAMs, scenarios and stress tests; compounded uncertainty and resolution limits.
Prioritise material disclosure gaps, issuer dialogue and engagement objectives.
Operational footprint and economic activity; shareholder rights; engagement limitations.
Cash-flow and discount-rate routes; avoid double counting; pass-through and sensitivity.
Scenario pathways → economic shocks → asset value streams → financial impacts; inspected as page image.
Contractual structure, issuer/guarantor boundaries, rates/spreads, default/recovery and rating materiality.
Use-of-proceeds versus SLBs; allocation, reporting, KPI calibration and verification.
Production/consumption accounting, GDP/population denominators, geography, fiscal capacity and currency.
Private-market differences are supporting context, not an added direct-investment mandate.
Financial goals versus climate outcomes, top-down/bottom-up integration and forward-looking metrics.
Define client beliefs, goals, constraints and relevant time horizon before implementation.
Accountability for mandate delivery, exposure, process, engagement and data limitations.
